newsitem.title: USA: CBS to launch Eye on People cable network.
newsitem.headline: CBS to launch Eye on People cable network.

text.p: CBS Cable will launch the CBS Eye on People cable network on March 31, CBS officials said Wednesday.
The basic cable, advertiser-supported, 24-hour network will offer entertainment and information programming, using prominent CBS network personalities CBS Cable executives said at a press conference.
Lloyd Werner, executive vice president of sales and marketing at CBS Cable, said CBS Eye on People "is not a news channel."
The network will be available in 2 million homes on March 31 and in 3 million homes by the end of April. It should have 10 million subscribers by the end of 1997, Werner said.

Noting that Time Warner Inc. cable systems will add 12 channels this year, Werner said CBS Eye on People is "under consideration" for one of those slots and CBS has been "led to believe that it's something they (Time Warner) want."
Werner said CBS Eye on People plans to announce next week the names of advertisers it has signed. The station will be promoted on CBS television and radio affiliates.
Geoffrey Darby, president of CBS Eye on People, said it would take five or six years for the new CBS cable network to stop losing money and 10 to 12 years "to get all your money back with interest."
CBS Cable, formerly Group W Satellite Communications, is a division of Westinghouse Electric Corp.'s Westinghouse/CBS.

Werner said that because this is a "very difficult time" in the cable industry, cable operators are taking "a wait and see attitude" toward new networks. But he called CBS Eye on People "better than anything cable has produced in a decade."

Several of the cable network's new series will capitalise on CBS News' existing programmes. "60 Minutes More," anchored by CBS correspondent Mike Wallace, will revisit and update segments from the "60 Minutes" magazine broadcast, and will have commentary by executive producer Don Hewitt.

Anchorwoman Paula Zahn will host a people-oriented programme, "Fast Forward" and Charles Kuralt will anchor "I Remember," a series of first-person accounts by CBS News correspondents of events they covered. The initial broadcast will look at the fall of Saigon with CBS News correspondents Ed Bradley and Bob Simon.
